elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 requires Vendor to “defend” Customer and its Affiliates from any third-party claim within the stated categories.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against losses resulting from the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 requires Vendor to indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates for resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the Services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) covers allegations that the Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) expressly extends the IP coverage to Deliverables.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(b) covers Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(d) expressly covers Vendor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require prompt notice by the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires the indemnified party to give prompt notice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must permit the indemnifying party to control the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires the indemnified party to allow the indemnifying party to control the defence.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation by the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 covers third-party claims to the extent arising from Customer-provided content.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 covers third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must not extend beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 states only those two triggers, and the original broad indemnity for every claim relating to Customer's use has been removed.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property infringement claims relating to the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) provides Vendor defence and indemnification for allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion for modifications made by Customer.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no combination exclusion.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion for compliance with Customer specifications.

elements.element: The IP remedies must require Vendor to procure the right to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 20.4 requires Vendor, at its expense, to procure the right to continue use.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit or require Vendor to modify the affected item so that it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: Section 20.4 includes modification so the affected item is non-infringing.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit or require Vendor to replace the affected item with a non-infringing item.
elements.evidence: Section 20.4 includes replacement with a non-infringing item.

elements.element: The IP remedies must require a refund if the continued-use, modification, or replacement remedies are not used.
elements.evidence: Section 20.4 includes refunding the Fees paid for the affected item as an alternative remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or super-cap appears in the rendered operative language.

result.reason: The rendered clause fully implements the preferred position: it gives Customer and its Affiliates the required Vendor indemnities, narrows Customer's indemnity to the two permitted triggers, and supplies standard procedures. The fallback is not independently complete because all three customary IP exclusions and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent, although its IP remedies are included. The changes are confined to the indemnity framework and the remedies needed to make the existing Section 9.3 cross-reference operative, without altering unrelated commercial terms.
